options.detail: QR opens Privilege Club/Avios award space on a rolling ~361-day window (longest in the industry; BA sees it ~355 days, AA ~331). Oct 10/11 2026 is only ~70 days out, so initial release happened long ago — the relevant pattern is QR's well-documented habit of releasing ADDITIONAL J seats closer to departure, and availability being 'often good at initial release, especially for flights from Doha.' Pricing: SIN-Europe runs ~70,000-75,000 Avios off-peak, 84,000-90,000 Avios peak one-way in J (QR added Peak/Off-Peak tiers covering ~1/3 of the year); Saver-tier seats on popular routes can vanish within hours of appearing, Flexi costs ~2x with better availability. Note two 2026 rule changes: Avios accounts must be 30 days old before transfers, and since June 2026 booking for others requires a pre-set Family & Friends/My List. Also, since Nov 2025 QR charges for seat selection on J award tickets. Could not verify live seat-map for Oct 10/11 specifically (seats.aero results require interactive search; no FlyerTalk date-specific report found in last 60 days).

options.label: (a) Comprehensive, family of 5, $45k trip — typical premium range
options.detail: Expect roughly $1,800-$3,600 total (4-8% of trip cost), with a young family (no traveler over 39) likely landing at the LOW end, ~$1,500-$2,500. Squaremouth's 2026 cruise data report (25,000+ purchases, Aug 2025-Aug 2026): comprehensive cruise plans average 6.9% of trip cost, but that skews older; ages 35-49 average $267/policy vs $637 at 65-69, and the $20,000+ trip-cost bracket averages $2,402/policy. options.label: (a) Best-in-class cruise pick #2: Nationwide Choice Cruise — cheap, but two catches
options.detail: Certificate (NWC2, NW Cruise Choice Ed. 04/2021, pulled today from travel.nationwide.com) confirms: Trip Cancellation 100% / Interruption 150% of trip cost, $100,000 medical, $500,000 emergency evacuation, Itinerary Change $500, Trip Interruption for Any Reason $500, plus cruise-specific Inconvenience benefit. Nationwide is consistently among the cheapest comprehensive cruise insurers — family estimate ~$1,200-$2,000. CATCH 1: medical is EXCESS/SECONDARY, not primary ('insurance provided by this Policy shall be in excess of all Other Insurance') — fails your primary-medical requirement. CATCH 2: the Missed Connection trigger is narrow (see option d).
options.source: https://travel.nationwide.com/certificate/NWC2/all.html (official certificate PDF, fetched and text-extracted 2026-08-01); https://www.forbes.com/advisor/travel-insurance/nationwide-travel-insurance-review/; https://www.insuremytrip.com/travel-insurance-reviews/providers/nationwide/choice-cruise-nwc2/
options.notes: Benefit facts confirmed from the certificate itself; premium is estimate. Note the certificate's Schedule lists Missed Connection max that PDF column-extraction maps to $1,500 (older reviews cite $500) — read the schedule on YOUR quote's certificate. CFAR is NOT offered on Choice Cruise — only on Nationwide Prime and Luxury Cruise plans (21-day window).

options.label: (b) Same trip + CFAR 75% — premium delta and eligibility windows
options.detail: CFAR adds ~48-52% to the premium. Squaremouth 2026 cruise data: comprehensive average $543 vs comprehensive+CFAR $806 (+48%); their separate 2026 stat puts the CFAR upcharge at ~52% average. Applied to your family: comprehensive ~$1,800-$3,000 becomes ~$2,700-$4,600 with CFAR; a $45k x 75% = $33,750 max CFAR payout. Eligibility windows (days from FIRST trip payment/deposit, all confirmed on current provider/aggregator pages): Travel Insured WTP 21 days; Travelex Ultimate 21 days; Nationwide (Prime/Luxury Cruise only) 21 days; Seven Corners Trip Protection Choice/Basic 20 days; IMG iTravelInsured SE/LX 20 days (Choice 21 days, but Choice caps trip cost at $10k/person — use LX, cap $150k/person). Universal conditions: insure 100% of nonrefundable costs, cancel 48+ hrs before departure, reimbursement 75% (not 100%). CRITICAL: the clock runs from your FIRST payment on the trip (likely the cruise deposit) — as of Aug 1, 2026, CFAR is only available if that first payment was made on/after ~July 11-12, 2026. If the cruise was deposited earlier, the CFAR window is already closed with every major insurer.
options.source: https://www.squaremouth.com/plans/cruise/cruise-insurance-cost ($543 vs $806); https://www.squaremouth.com/resources/best-travel-insurance/cancel-for-any-reason (21-day windows); https://www.insuremytrip.com/travel-insurance-plans-coverages/cancel-for-any-reason/ (IMG 20/21-day windows + per-person caps); https://www.forbes.com/advisor/travel-insurance/best-cancel-for-any-reason-travel-insurance/ (Travelex 21 days); https://www.sevencorners.com/plans/trip-protection (20 days)
options.notes: Status 'confirmed' = the delta percentage and windows are from current primary/aggregator pages; the dollar figure is derived. CFAR not available to NY/WA residents on some plans — CA is fine. Some sources say 14 days for Travel Insured's Deluxe tier vs 21 for Platinum/WTP; the flagship WTP and FlexiPAX are 21.

options.label: (c) Annual multi-trip alternative — RULED OUT for the $45k trip
options.detail: No mainstream annual policy comes close to $45,000 of trip-cancellation cover. Allianz AllTrips Executive (the highest-cancellation annual plan Allianz sells): trip cancellation/interruption tiers of $5,000, $7,500, or $10,000 PER PERSON PER YEAR (all trips combined), 45-day max trip length; AllTrips Premier tops out at $15,000/year. Allianz's own guidance for exceeding the cap is to buy a separate single-trip plan. Annual plans (~$249-$500/person/yr for Executive tiers) remain sensible only as a medical/evac-only layer for the frequent-traveling adult — they cannot replace a single-trip policy for cancellation on this trip.
options.source: https://www.allianztravelinsurance.com/travel/annual (official); https://www.allianztravelinsurance.com/travel/annual/annual-travel-insurance-reaching-coverage-limit.htm (official: caps are annual, buy separate plan if exceeded); https://www.usnews.com/insurance/travel/allianz-travel (tier amounts, 45-day trip limit)
options.notes: price_usd 0 = not a viable option for this need, no premium quoted. Verdict: caps ($5k-$15k) categorically rule out annual policies for a $45k trip cost.

options.label: (d) 'Missed connection — join ship at next port' fine print, by insurer
options.detail: Insurers that explicitly pay transportation to catch up to the ship: (1) SEVEN CORNERS Trip Protection Choice and Cruise plans — highest benefit found, $1,500 ($250/day), Squaremouth describes it as 'designed to cover new travel arrangements and catching up with your cruise at the next port,' 3-hr delay trigger. (2) TRAVEL INSURED WTP — $500 ($1,000 with upgrade), cruise/tour-only, 3-hr common-carrier delay trigger, pays 'additional transportation expenses to join your departed cruise.' (3) TRAVELEX Ultimate — $750, and their assistance line 'can help arrange transportation to the next port'; 21-day CFAR window. (4) NATIONWIDE Choice Cruise — certificate language confirmed today: pays 'additional transportation expenses needed for You to join Your departed Cruise' BUT the Missed Connection trigger is ONLY weather-caused cancellation/delay (3-6 hrs) of ALL regularly scheduled flights, and is secondary to airline compensation. A mechanical delay or ATC meltdown does NOT trigger it — though Nationwide's separate Trip Delay benefit (6+ hr, broader hazard list) pays an economy fare 'to a destination where You can catch up to the Trip.' (5) BERKSHIRE HATHAWAY WaveCare — cruise-specific plan with missed-connection + $750,000 evac (their highest), plus disabled-ship and diversion benefits.
options.source: https://travel.nationwide.com/certificate/NWC2/all.html (certificate text, primary source); https://www.squaremouth.com/travel-insurance-benefits/missed-connection (Seven Corners $1,500 ranking); https://www.sevencorners.com/plans/cruise; https://www.travelexinsurance.com/travel-insurance/benefits/missed-connections (official); https://www.travelinsured.com/benefits/missed-connection (official); https://www.bhtp.com/travel-insurance/wavecare/
options.notes: Practical read: all missed-connection caps ($500-$1,500) are small vs the real cost of flying a family of 5 to a foreign port mid-cruise. The bigger levers are Trip Delay + Trip Interruption (Nationwide pays 150% of trip cost on interruption; WTP similar). Board a day early regardless — every insurer's trigger assumes a covered common-carrier/weather delay, never a tight self-booked connection.

options.label: (e) Separate single adult, Sept 27-Oct 28 (~32 days, ~$12k flights)
options.detail: Comprehensive single-trip for a 39-year-old, $12,000 trip cost, ~32 days: expect ~$480-$850 (4-7%); Squaremouth's $10,001-$20,000 trip-cost bracket averages $967 across all ages/cruise trips, and the 35-49 age band averages well below overall means, so ~$550-$700 is the realistic center. With CFAR 75% (~+50%): ~$720-$1,275, subject to the same 20-21-day-from-first-payment window — if those flights were ticketed more than 21 days ago, CFAR is unavailable. If the $12k is airfare that's largely credit-eligible on cancellation, consider insuring only the truly nonrefundable portion (premium scales with declared trip cost) plus a strong medical/evac plan.
options.source: https://www.squaremouth.com/plans/cruise/cruise-insurance-cost (trip-cost and age brackets); https://www.squaremouth.com/travel-advice/cost-for-travel-insurance (4-10% rule, ~6% average); https://www.experian.com/blogs/ask-experian/average-travel-insurance-cost/
options.notes: Trip length pushes cost up (15-30 day trips average $929 in Squaremouth cruise data), but low trip cost per day and age 39 pull it back down. Airlines' own refund/credit rules matter more than insurance for pure-airfare trips.

summary: Family of 5, $45k, Oct 8-28: budget ~$1,500-$2,500 for a best-in-class comprehensive policy (Squaremouth 2026 cruise data: 6.9% avg of trip cost, but your young ages and kids-free provisions pull you under 4-5%). Best fit for the stated spec (primary medical + $500k evac + cruise missed-connection): Travel Insured Worldwide Trip Protector ($100k primary medical, $1M evac, kids 17-and-under free, 21-day CFAR window, missed connection pays to join the departed cruise) at an estimated ~$1,300-$2,200. Nationwide Choice Cruise is the cheapest strong cruise plan (~$1,200-$2,000, $500k evac confirmed from its certificate) but its medical is EXCESS not primary and its missed-connection trigger is weather-only — and CFAR isn't offered on Choice (only Prime/Luxury Cruise). CFAR 75% adds ~48-52% (family total ~$2,700-$4,600) and is ONLY purchasable within 20-21 days of the FIRST trip payment — as of Aug 1, that means first payment on/after ~July 11, 2026, or the window is closed everywhere. Annual plans are definitively ruled out for cancellation: Allianz AllTrips Executive caps at $10k/person/year (Premier $15k), per Allianz's own pages. Highest explicit catch-up-to-next-port benefit found: Seven Corners at $1,500 ($250/day). Single adult Sept 27-Oct 28 ($12k): ~$550-$700 comprehensive, ~$800-$1,100 with CFAR.
caveats: No insurer publishes bindable premiums without running their quote engine (age/state/trip-cost rated), so every dollar premium here is an aggregator-derived estimate, not a live quote — 30 minutes on Squaremouth/TravelInsurance.com with exact DOBs and the $45,000 figure will produce real numbers, and I'd expect them inside the ranges given. CFAR eligibility is the time-critical item: the clock started at the cruise deposit, not at booking of later components — if that deposit predates ~July 11, 2026, drop CFAR from the plan and lean on Trip Interruption (150% on Nationwide) plus 'Interruption for Any Reason' riders instead.
